SMTO-EXE-0245 — SMTO got an unreadable answer from Docker

GUID: e9037b49-8cf8-5929-97a8-0986a16d65c2
Slug: docker-invalid-response
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: docker

What happened

  • The answer that came back from Docker or the Gateway was damaged, too large, or in a form SMTO doesn't understand, so SMTO didn't use it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you had asked for a change, ask SMTO to show the current state of the containers, images or project involved, without changing anything. The error alone does not establish whether the change happened, so looking at the current state tells you.
  2. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check for updates. If an update is offered, install it when no other tasks are running there, because updating restarts the Gateway. A Gateway on a different version from SMTO can send answers SMTO doesn't recognise.
  3. If the change isn't already there, ask SMTO to try the request once more. If the same unreadable answer comes back, the problem isn't a one-off and needs to be reported.

What success looks like

  • The same request now returns a normal result in the task.

If it still fails

  • Open Technical details in this panel, select Copy error details, and send them to the person who manages SMTO; this is likely a bug they need to report. Don't repeat a change over and over while this error keeps appearing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Docker response validation rejected the result: oversized or malformed Engine or Gateway data, bad stream/multiplex framing, invalid Buildx cache fields, or a Gateway receipt or cancel acknowledgement incompatible with the server's Docker contract.

What this means

  • Docker wire validation rejected oversized/malformed result data, bad stream/multiplex framing, invalid cache fields or an incompatible Gateway/control receipt. Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.

Why this can happen

  • Docker wire validation rejected oversized/malformed result data, bad stream/multiplex framing, invalid cache fields or an incompatible Gateway/control receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify Engine stream versus Gateway receipt validation and retain whether any mutation had already begun.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the structural diagnostics in the receipt and check that the Gateway and server versions match (Settings › Setup › Gateways › Check for updates). If the request was a change, inspect Engine state read-only before any new mutation. Report reproducible malformed Engine or Buildx output as a bug with the copied error details.
  • Inspect structural response diagnostics and existing Engine state; repair the demonstrated protocol problem before new mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the exact object identity, typed arguments and selected Gateway capability; correct the reported prerequisite before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • Original effects are reconciled and the relevant protocol returns a valid bounded result.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain Docker mutation.

Technical notes

  • Docker execution remains on the selected Gateway and its explicitly configured local Engine. Preserve accepted private references, exact object identities, completed prefixes and unknown effects; diagnostics never replay a mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
